status: DRAFT answer key: written with the corpus, to be reviewed and signed off by the author before results are reported.
matching: Findings are matched by the provisions they cite, not by requirement id. The best candidate is the finding whose citations are most focused on the listed provisions.

requirements.why: The practice (custodian) is established in Subregion A1, listed in Annex I.
Art 8(2)(c) health-care condition on the basis of Subregion law.
A1-HIA 4(1) registered practitioners; 4(2) an agent on documented instructions is under their responsibility. Needs delegation.
6(1)(b) contract: patients pay under terms of care.
The signed agreement covers the 9(2) terms; its deletion term interacts with B-HRA 9 (see conflicts).
No route covers the transfer as described: recognition excludes sensitive data, derogations exclude ongoing transfers, and the approved clauses fail Art 18(2)-(3) while Northgate holds the keys.
Cumulative A1 condition: 30 days' notice to the Commission (not given) and keys held only in Region A (held by Northgate in Region B). Needs delegation.
3,200 patients is below the A-REG 12(2)(a) threshold, but A1-HIA 8(a) requires an assessment for hosting a patient record system outside A1 regardless of numbers; none was prepared.
The notice names the third territory and the route relied on.
Northgate is a data host; it must keep records 7 years unless it returns foreign-origin records and keeps no copy. The agreement says delete within 30 days.
The practice bills no Region B insurer, so it is not a covered provider and Northgate is not its service agent (B-HRA 3(2)).

routes.why: Annex II recognition of Region B extends only to non-sensitive information, despite the active certificate.
Executed clauses plus a documented 18(2) assessment and keys held only in Region A (B-RAA 5 then removes compelled decryption) would cover the transfer.
The transfer is ongoing, so 19(1)(a)-(b) are excluded by 19(2); (c) and (d) do not fit.
Patients pay under terms of care.
B-HRA 9(2): returning foreign-origin records at the end of service and keeping no copy satisfies the retention rule; A-REG 9(2)(f) lets the custodian choose return.

conflicts.why: Choose return rather than deletion under A-REG 9(2)(f); returning foreign-origin records and keeping no copy satisfies B-HRA 9(2).

questions.why: Art 18(2) needs Region B's law on public-authority access (B-RAA 3-6), which only the Region B specialist can read.

must_not.why: Treating the Trusted Recipient certificate as an Art 17 route for health records.
Relying on a derogation for an ongoing hosting arrangement.
Relying on legitimate interests for health records.
No ground relies on consent, so child-consent age rules are not engaged.
